entries.relies: The Worker is deployed under the name in the configuration file.
entries.evidence: The name of your Worker. Alphanumeric characters ( `a`, `b`, `c`, etc.) and dashes ( `-`) only.

entries.relies: `main` names the Worker entry file that exports the `fetch` and `email` handlers.
entries.evidence: The path to the entrypoint of your Worker that will be executed.

entries.relies: The date selects the runtime behaviour: every compatibility flag with a default date up to it is on.
entries.evidence: by specifying a `compatibility_date` for your Worker, you can quickly enable all of these various compatibility flags up to, and including, that date.

entries.relies: Node.js built-in modules and polyfills are available to the Worker and its dependencies without a compatibility flag, because the compatibility date is 2026-08-04 or later.
entries.evidence: For compatibility dates of `2026-08-04` or later, Workers enables both `nodejs_compat` and `nodejs_compat_v2` by default.
entries.note: `wrangler.jsonc` sets no `nodejs_compat` flag. Moving the compatibility date below 2026-08-04 would need the flag back.

entries.relies: `observability.enabled` makes the Worker write its logs to Workers Logs.
entries.evidence: You must add the observability setting for your Worker to write logs to Workers Logs.

entries.relies: A request that matches no asset is answered with `/index.html`, so the single-page app handles its own routes.
entries.evidence: When an incoming request does not match a file in the `assets.directory`, Workers will serve the contents of the `/index.html` file with a `200 OK` status.

entries.relies: Only the listed route patterns (`/api/*`, `/mcp`, `/agents/*`) reach the Worker before the assets.
entries.evidence: You can also specify `run_worker_first` as an array of route patterns to selectively run the Worker script first only for specific routes.

entries.relies: `vars` sets plain environment variables (the domains, the address allow-list, the feature switches).
entries.evidence: A map of environment variables to set when deploying your Worker.

entries.relies: A `send_email` entry with only a `name` gives the Worker the `EMAIL` send binding.
entries.evidence: Configure a `send_email` binding in your Wrangler configuration file to enable email sending:
entries.note: The send bindings page describes an entry without a restriction attribute as able to send to any verified destination address. The pricing page says arbitrary recipients need Workers Paid.

entries.relies: An `r2_buckets` entry binds the bucket as `BUCKET`.
entries.evidence: To bind R2 buckets to your Worker, assign an array of the below object to the `r2_buckets` key.

entries.relies: The `ai` key binds Workers AI as `AI`. Only the optional agent features use it.
entries.evidence: Unlike other bindings, this binding is limited to one AI binding per Worker project.

entries.relies: `durable_objects.bindings` binds each Durable Object class by `name` and `class_name`.
entries.evidence: To bind Durable Objects to your Worker, assign an array of the below object to the `durable_objects.bindings` key.

entries.relies: Each Durable Object class is created with the SQLite storage backend by a `new_sqlite_classes` migration.
entries.evidence: The `migrations` array remains fully supported for existing Workers and continues to work as documented here.
entries.note: The page calls `migrations` legacy and prefers the declarative `exports` field for new Workers. The two cannot be mixed for Durable Objects.

entries.relies: Inbound mail reaches the Worker through the exported `email(message, env, ctx)` handler.
entries.evidence: Add the `email` handler function to your Worker's exported handlers:

entries.relies: `message.from` is the envelope sender, not the `From:` header.
entries.evidence: readonly from: string; // Sender email address (envelope MAIL FROM)

entries.relies: `message.to` is the envelope recipient. Podbay files a message by it and never by the `To:` header.
entries.evidence: readonly to: string; // Recipient email address (envelope RCPT TO)

entries.relies: `message.raw` is a stream of the raw MIME message.
entries.evidence: readonly raw: ReadableStream; // Raw MIME email content stream

entries.relies: `message.rawSize` is the size of the raw message in bytes. Podbay sizes its read buffer from it.
entries.evidence: readonly rawSize: number; // Size of raw email in bytes

entries.relies: `message.setReject(reason)` refuses the message with a permanent SMTP error. Podbay calls it for an unknown recipient.
entries.evidence: Reject emails with a permanent SMTP error:

entries.relies: Only the first `Authentication-Results` header, written by `mx.cloudflare.net`, can be trusted for SPF, DKIM and DMARC results.
entries.evidence: Other `Authentication-Results` headers may have been supplied by the sender and should not be trusted.

entries.relies: `env.EMAIL.send(message)` takes a structured message and resolves to a result.
entries.evidence: send(message: EmailMessage | EmailMessageBuilder): Promise<EmailSendResult>;

entries.relies: The message takes `to`, `from`, `subject`, `html`, `text`, `cc`, `bcc` and `replyTo`. An address is a string or `{ email, name }`.
entries.evidence: to: string | EmailAddress | (string | EmailAddress)[]; // Max 50 recipients

entries.relies: An attachment is `{ content, filename, type, disposition, contentId? }`. Podbay passes `content` as a base64 string.
entries.evidence: content: string | ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView; // Base64 string or binary content

entries.relies: Custom headers are passed as a `headers` map of strings.
entries.evidence: headers?: { [key: string]: string };

entries.relies: A successful send returns `{ messageId }`. A failed send throws an `Error` with a `code` property.
entries.evidence: // Errors are thrown as standard Error objects with a `code` property

entries.relies: `bucket.get(key)` returns the object with its body, or `null` when the key does not exist.
entries.evidence: `get` `(key: string, options?: R2GetOptions): Promise<R2ObjectBody | R2Object | null>`

entries.relies: `bucket.put(key, value)` stores a string or bytes under the key.
entries.evidence: Stores the given `value` and metadata under the associated `key`. Once the write succeeds, returns an `R2Object` containing metadata about the stored Object.

entries.relies: `bucket.delete(key)` removes an object, and later reads no longer see it.
entries.evidence: R2 deletes are strongly consistent. Once the Promise resolves, all subsequent read operations will no longer see the provided key value pairs globally.

entries.relies: `namespace.idFromName(name)` always gives the same id for a name, and `namespace.get(id)` gives a stub. One Durable Object per mailbox address.
entries.evidence: Named Durable Objects are the most common method of referring to Durable Objects.

entries.relies: `ctx.storage.sql.exec(query, ...bindings)` runs SQL with `?` placeholders and returns an iterable cursor of rows.
entries.evidence: `exec(query: string, ...bindings: any[])`: `SqlStorageCursor`

entries.relies: `ctx.storage.transactionSync(callback)` runs synchronous SQL in one transaction and rolls back when the callback throws. Migrations use it because `sql.exec` cannot run `BEGIN TRANSACTION`.
entries.evidence: Note that `sql.exec()` cannot execute transaction-related statements like `BEGIN TRANSACTION` or `SAVEPOINT`.

entries.relies: SQLite in a Durable Object includes the FTS5 module. The planned mailbox search index is built on it.
entries.evidence: for full-text search (including `fts5vocab`).

entries.relies: `ctx.waitUntil(promise)` lets work continue after the handler has returned. Podbay sends mail and wakes the agent this way.
entries.evidence: `ctx.waitUntil()` extends the lifetime of your Worker, allowing you to perform work without blocking returning a response, and that may continue after a response is returned.

entries.relies: Cloudflare Access puts the application token in the `Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion` request header. The Worker checks its signature, issuer and audience.
entries.evidence: If you need to validate the JWT manually, read it from the `Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion` header.

entries.relies: The signing keys of an Access team are served at `/cdn-cgi/access/certs` on the team domain.
entries.evidence: The public key for the signing key pair is located at `https://<your-team-name>.cloudflareaccess.com/cdn-cgi/access/certs`

entries.relies: `ai.run(model, input)` runs a Workers AI model. Only the optional agent features call it.
entries.evidence: `async env.AI.run()` runs a model. Takes a model as the first parameter, and an object as the second parameter.

entries.relies: `@cf/zai-org/glm-4.7-flash` is a Workers AI chat model with tool calling that needs no paid plan. It is the assistant's chat model.
entries.evidence: Optimized for dialogue, instruction-following, and multi-turn tool calling across 100+ languages.
entries.note: The page states the model id, `Function calling | Yes`, `Reasoning | Yes`, $0.0605 per M input and $0.40 per M output tokens, and carries no paid-access or planned-deprecation label. The changelog of 2026-07-28 names it among the models that remain on the Workers Free plan. It replaces `@cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.5`, which the changelog of 2026-05-08 aliased to `kimi-k2.6` from 2026-05-30; `kimi-k2.6` needs the Workers Paid plan and is retired on 2026-11-20.

entries.relies: `@cf/ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-micro` is a Workers AI text model that accepts chat messages and answers in a `response` string. It runs the prompt-injection scan.
entries.evidence: const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-micro", { messages });
entries.note: The page's output schema is `response` (string), `usage`, `tool_calls`; it lists no reasoning, $0.017 per M input and $0.112 per M output tokens (the lowest text-model row on the pricing page), and no paid-access or planned-deprecation label. It replaces `@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fast`: on 2026-11-17 that model page returns 404 and the catalog does not list the id, although the changelog of 2026-05-08 said the `-fast` variants remain active.

entries.relies: `@cf/meta/llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct` is a Workers AI text model that accepts chat messages and answers in a `response` string. It runs the draft verifier.
entries.evidence: const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/meta/llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct", { messages });
entries.note: The page's output schema is `response` (string), `usage`, `tool_calls`; it lists no reasoning, $0.27 per M input and $0.85 per M output tokens, and no paid-access or planned-deprecation label.

entries.relies: Cloudflare retires Workers AI model ids on announced dates; a retired id fails every request. None of the three ids in `workers/lib/models.ts` is on the list for 2026-11-20.
entries.evidence: Starting November 20, 2026, these models will stop returning responses. Requests to them will fail with an HTTP `410 Gone` error
entries.note: The error is code `5028`. The list names `@cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6`, `@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fp8` and 14 other text models. When a model call fails, the injection scan blocks the automatic draft and the draft verifier refuses the draft (both fail closed), so a retired id stops the assistant from drafting but sends and leaks nothing. Read the Workers AI changelog before each release.

entries.relies: In local development and in tests every binding is a local simulation, so no real mail is sent. Workers AI is the exception and stays off.
entries.evidence: By default, bindings connect to **local resource simulations** (except for [AI bindings](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/bindings/), as AI models always run remotely).

entries.relies: The local `send_email` binding logs a message and does not send it.
entries.evidence: By default, `wrangler dev` simulates the email binding locally. It logs emails to the console but does not send them.
entries.note: The page names `wrangler dev`. Podbay runs the Vite plugin, and the page does not mention it.

entries.relies: A raw message posted to `/cdn-cgi/local/email?from=…&to=…` on the local server is delivered to the `email` handler.
entries.evidence: curl --request POST 'http://localhost:8787/cdn-cgi/local/email' \
entries.note: An older path, `/cdn-cgi/handler/email`, still works in the installed Vite plugin as a legacy route; Podbay's docs use the documented one.

entries.relies: The Vite plugin's `viteEnvironment.name` option names the Vite environment the Worker runs in.
entries.evidence: By default, the environment name is the Worker name with `-` characters replaced with `_`. Setting the name here will override this.

entries.relies: `cloudflareTest({ wrangler: { configPath } })` loads the entry point, the compatibility settings and the bindings from `wrangler.jsonc`.
entries.evidence: `wrangler`: `{ configPath?: string; environment?: string; }` optional

entries.relies: `cloudflareTest({ remoteBindings: false })` keeps every binding local. The option is on by default.
entries.evidence: remoteBindings: z.boolean().default(true),
entries.note: The docs page for the Vitest integration does not list this option, so the source is the plugin's own code.

entries.relies: An inbound message is at most 25 MiB. Larger mail never reaches the Worker.
entries.evidence: | **Inbound message size** | 25 MiB | Messages larger than this are rejected |

entries.relies: A message being sent is at most 25 MiB in all, attachments included, and goes to at most 50 recipients. The Worker refuses more before it stores or sends anything, and the app says so while the message is written.
entries.evidence: | **Total message size** | 25 MiB | Including attachments |
entries.note: The same table: `| **Recipients (to, cc, bcc)** | 50 per email | Combined across all recipient fields |`.

entries.relies: A Durable Object can set one alarm at a time; it runs at least once and is retried when the handler throws. Proposed for waking snoozed mail (ADR-0010): many times are kept in storage, and the alarm is set to the earliest.
entries.evidence: Each Durable Object is able to schedule a single alarm at a time by calling `setAlarm()`.
entries.note: The same page: `Alarms have guaranteed at-least-once execution and are retried automatically when the alarm() handler throws.` Nothing uses an alarm yet.

entries.relies: One Durable Object stores at most 10 GB, so raw messages and attachments live in R2.
entries.evidence: 10 GB on Workers Paid, or 1 GB on the Free plan
entries.note: 10 GB holds on Workers Paid only. On the Free plan one Durable Object stores 1 GB and the account 5 GB in total.

entries.relies: A string, a blob or a table row in a Durable Object is at most 8 MB.
entries.evidence: | Maximum string, `BLOB` or table row size | 8 MB |

entries.relies: One query in a Durable Object takes at most 100 bound parameters and a statement is at most 100 KB, so a change to many messages at once (labelling a selection) is made in batches.
entries.evidence: | Maximum bound parameters per query | 100 |

entries.relies: A `LIKE` pattern is at most 50 bytes. The mailbox search builds `LIKE` patterns from the search text.
entries.evidence: | Maximum characters (bytes) in a `LIKE` or `GLOB` pattern | 50 bytes |

entries.relies: A SQLite-backed Durable Object can be restored to any point in the past 30 days.
entries.evidence: restore a Durable Object's embedded SQLite database to any point in time in the past 30 days.

entries.relies: A queue message is at most 128 KB, so the planned inbound queue carries a pointer and not the message.
entries.evidence: | Message size | 128 KB <sup>1</sup> |
entries.note: The page counts 1 KB as 1000 bytes, and up to about 100 bytes of internal metadata count towards the limit.

entries.relies: An isolate has 128 MB of memory, on every plan.
entries.evidence: | Memory per isolate | 128 MB |

entries.relies: Cloudflare documents Email Sending as a beta.
entries.evidence: **Email Sending** Beta sends outbound transactional emails. Available on Workers Paid plan

entries.relies: Sending to any recipient needs the Workers Paid plan.
entries.evidence: Sending to arbitrary recipients requires the Workers Paid plan.

entries.relies: Workers Paid includes 3,000 outbound mails a month. After that the price is $0.35 per 1,000.
entries.evidence: 3,000 included per month, then $0.35 per 1,000 emails

entries.relies: On Workers Free, Podbay can still send to the account's verified destination addresses, at no charge.
entries.evidence: Sends to verified destination addresses are free and do not count toward the included quota.

entries.relies: Receiving mail works on Workers Free and on Workers Paid.
entries.evidence: Email Routing is available on both the Workers Free and Workers Paid plans.

entries.relies: A D1 database is bound as `env.DB`; it holds accounts, sessions, mailboxes, memberships and the audit log.
entries.evidence: "binding": "prod_d1_tutorial", // available in your Worker on env.DB
entries.note: `migrations_dir` on the same binding points at `migrations/` (source: https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/reference/migrations/, page updated 2026-06-08).

entries.relies: Statements passed to `batch()` run as one transaction: all of them apply or none does. Podbay uses it wherever writes belong together, because D1 has no interactive transactions.
entries.evidence: Batched statements are [SQL transactions ↗︎](https://www.sqlite.org/lang_transaction.html).

entries.relies: Foreign keys are enforced, so deleting a mailbox removes its memberships and deleting a user removes their roles and memberships.
entries.evidence: By default, D1 enforces that foreign key constraints are valid within all queries and migrations.

entries.relies: A `_headers` file in the asset directory adds response headers to static assets; it does not apply to responses the Worker generates, so the Worker sets the same headers itself.
entries.evidence: Custom headers defined in the `_headers` file are not applied to responses generated by your Worker code, even if the request URL matches a rule defined in `_headers`.

entries.relies: The MCP endpoint is `createMcpHandler` from `agents/mcp/server` around an MCP SDK v2 server built for one request: no Durable Object and no protocol session, so nothing outlives the key check made for that request.
entries.evidence: The handler is stateless: it builds a fresh server for every request, so you do not need a Durable Object, protocol session, or WebSocket.

entries.relies: The handler refuses a browser Origin that is not allowed; Podbay allows only the hostname the request came to and removes the CORS headers (`corsOptions: false`), so no other site's page can use the endpoint. Clients that send no Origin still work.
entries.evidence: The Workers wrapper validates every present browser Origin. It rejects malformed, opaque, and non-HTTP Origins with `403`. Origin-less non-browser MCP clients remain valid.
entries.note: The page says a custom domain with wildcard CORS must set `allowedHostnames` and `allowedOriginHostnames` itself; Podbay sets the Origin list on every request and sends no CORS headers.

entries.relies: The sign-in rate limits count attempts per client address, read from `cf-connecting-ip`, which Cloudflare sets on the request to the Worker; a client cannot choose it the way it can prepend to `x-forwarded-for`.
entries.evidence: When no Worker subrequest is triggered, `cf-connecting-ip` reflects the client's IP address and the `x-real-ip` header is stripped.
entries.note: The page also says that another Worker in front, on the same zone, can alter `x-real-ip` and with it this header. An instance placed behind such a Worker must trust it.

entries.relies: A storage key ends with the file's name, so a name is cut to 255 bytes before it becomes part of a key: a longer key would make the write fail, and with it the delivery of the message that carries the file.
entries.evidence: Object key length | 1,024 bytes

entries.relies: A message being sent carries at most 32 files; the request is refused before anything is stored, and the app says so while the person writes.
entries.evidence: `attachments` array exceeds 32 entries
